test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: ________ method is especially suited to mines, oil wells. quarries, sandpits and similar assets of a wasting character.
solution:
The correct answer is** Depletion.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Depletion method is especially suited to mines, oil wells, quarries, sandpits and similar assets of a wasting character:**

 
 
• Depletion refers to the allocation of the cost of natural resources over time as they are extracted and used.
 
• This method is particularly relevant for industries involved in the extraction of natural resources, such as mining, oil drilling, and quarrying.
 
• It ensures that the expense associated with the asset's usage is matched with the revenue generated from the sale of the extracted resources.
 
• Depletion can be calculated using either the cost depletion method or the percentage depletion method.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amortisation:**

 
 
• Amortisation is the process of spreading the cost of an intangible asset over its useful life.
 
• It is typically applied to assets such as patents, trademarks, and goodwill.
 
• Since mines, oil wells, and quarries are tangible assets, amortisation is not the appropriate method for these.
 
 
 
• **Depreciation:**
 
 
• Depreciation is the systematic allocation of the cost of a tangible fixed asset over its useful life.
 
• It is used for assets like machinery, buildings, and vehicles.
 
• While similar to depletion, depreciation is not specifically designed for wasting natural resources.
 
 
 
• **Dilapidation:**
 
 
• Dilapidation refers to the state of disrepair or deterioration of a building or structure due to neglect or misuse.
 
• It is not a method of cost allocation and thus is not relevant to the context of natural resource extraction.
